claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child I'm responsible for. My son Alex is 15 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You have a son Alex who is 15 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now let me ask:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, there is another person who's also responsible for Alex - his other parent. We can't seem to agree on who should claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important detail.

According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. If you and Alex's other parent are both responsible for him and cannot agree on who should claim, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will decide who will get it.

Before I make my final assessment, let me ask one more question:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training, or does he work 24 hours or more per week, or does he claim any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. He doesn't work that many hours, he's not claiming any benefits himself, and he's not in any approved education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me summarize what you've told me:

- Alex is 15 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you
- You are responsible for Alex
- Alex's other parent is also responsible for him, and you cannot agree on who should claim
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week, not claiming benefits, and not in approved education or training
- No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Based on the UK Child Benefit rules, here is my assessment:

You would be **eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex because:
- He is under 16 years old
- You live in the UK
- You are responsible for him and he lives with you

However, there's an important point: since you and Alex's other parent cannot agree on who should claim, if both of you were to apply, HMRC would make the decision about who receives the Child Benefit. Only one person can receive it for the same child.

The fact that Alex is not currently in approved education or training doesn't affect eligibility at age 15, though this will become relevant when he turns 16.

You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you'd like to proceed with a claim, you can apply online or by post. If the other parent also applies, HMRC will make the final decision about who receives the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
